BoxplotSCI

Source: vignettes/boxplotSCI.Rmd
boxplotSCI.Rmd

The function boxplotSCI() generates boxplots of a variable of interest (such as a quality of life score, for example) for one time point or over time for one or two groups.

Setup and data

To demonstrate the various functionalities, we will use the dataset summarySCI::hemoglobin_data.

library(summarySCI)
data(hemoglobin_data)
hemoglobin <- hemoglobin_data

The dataset hemoglobin contains the hemoglobin values of 169 patients at 9 different time points. The time points in the column visit_nr are coded as numeric, while the time points in column visit are coded as factor. The column Arm indicates whether the patient was in Arm A or Arm B.

head(hemoglobin)
#>    ID   Arm   visit visit_nr  hb
#> 1 ID1 Arm B Cycle 9        9 132
#> 2 ID1 Arm B Cycle 8        8 130
#> 3 ID1 Arm B Cycle 7        7 135
#> 4 ID1 Arm B Cycle 6        6 140
#> 5 ID1 Arm B Cycle 5        5 139
#> 6 ID1 Arm B Cycle 4        4 138

Basic boxplots for two groups 

boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  main = "Boxplots for the two groups", 
                  legend_position = "topleft")

Now let us imagine that we want the order of the treatment groups to be reversed.

hemoglobin$Arm <- factor(hemoglobin$Arm, levels = c("Arm B", 
                                                "Arm A"))

boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  main = "Reversed treatment order", 
                  legend_position = "topright")

Group names

The names of the two groups can be customized using group_names (for the legend) and group_names_short for the x-axis. The order in group_names and group_names_short must match the order of levels(factor(data$group))

# back to original order
hemoglobin$Arm <- factor(hemoglobin$Arm, levels = c("Arm A", 
                                                "Arm B"))

boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                  group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                  main = "Customization of group names", 
                  legend_position = "topright")

One group

The function can also be used when there is only one group.

boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin[hemoglobin$Arm == "Arm A", ], # Only treatment
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr,
                  main = "Only treatment group")

Time points as factors

The function also accept time points given as factors. In this case, the user needs to make sure that the factor is correctly ordered.

hemoglobin$visit <- factor(hemoglobin$visit,
                           levels = c("Cycle 1", "Cycle 2", "Cycle 3", 
                                      "Cycle 4", "Cycle 5", "Cycle 6", 
                                      "Cycle 7", "Cycle 8", "Cycle 9"))
boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                  group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                  main = "Time points as factor", 
                  legend_position = "topleft"
                  )

Another equivalent alternative is to put the numeric time points in order and the labels in visit.


boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr, 
                  visit = visit,
                  group = Arm, 
                  group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                  group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                  main = "Time points as factor", 
                  legend_position = "topleft"
                  )

Customization of the boxplots

Legend

The position and size of the legend can easily be adapted using the arguments legend_position and legend_cex, respectively. A box can be added around the legend using legend_bty = "o".

boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  # short names
                  group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                  group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                  # Title
                  main = "Hemoglobin over time", 
                  # Legend position
                  legend_position = "bottomright",
                  # Legend size
                  legend_cex = 0.75, 
                  # Legend box
                  legend_bty = "o"
                  )

Size and color of boxes

The color and size of the boxes can be customized using the arguments col and boxwex. The distance between the boxes (when two groups are compared) can be adjusted with the argument shift.


boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  # short names
                  group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                  group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                  # Title
                  main = "Hemoglobin over time", 
                  # Col of boxes
                  col = c("lightblue", "orange"),
                  # Width of boxes
                  boxwex = 0.2, 
                  #Space between boxes
                  shift = 0.15,
                  # Legend position
                  legend_position = "topleft",
                  )

Axes

Various parameters related to the axes can be customized using xlab, ylab, cex_lab, cex_axis, ylim and y_ticks.

par(las = 1)
boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                  group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                  # Title
                  main = "Hemoglobin over time", 
                  # X axis label
                  xlab = "Visits", 
                  # X axis position
                  xlab_position = 0,
                  # Y axis label
                  ylab = "Score",
                  # Size of axis labels
                  cex_lab = 1.2,
                  # Size of axes
                  cex_axis = 1.1,
                  # Size of number of patients
                  cex_n_patients = 0.9,
                  # Y axis limit
                  ylim = c(80, 200),
                  # Y axis ticks
                  y_ticks = seq(80, 180, by = 10),
                  legend_position = "topleft"
                  )

Lines and colors

Lines can be added using lines and their color and type specified using col_lines and lty, respectively.


boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin, 
                  var = hb, 
                  order = visit_nr, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                  group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                  # Title
                  main = "Hemoglobin over time", 
                  # Col of boxes
                  col = c("lightblue", "orange"),
                  # X axis label
                  xlab = "Visits", 
                  # X axis position
                  xlab_position = 0,
                  # Y axis label
                  ylab = "Score",
                  lines = c(90, 120, 160), 
                  # Col of lines
                  col_lines = c("red", "grey", "red"), 
                  # Type of lines
                  lty = c(2, 3, 2)
                  )

Special case: only one time point

The function also works if no intput is provided for order or if order only contains one time point.

par(las = 1)
boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin[hemoglobin$visit_nr == 4, ], 
                  var = hb, 
                  # order = visit_nr, 
                  group = Arm, 
                  main = "Only one time point"
                  )

Time point is missing for one group

The function also works if one (or more) time points are missing for one of the groups. The argument missing_nr controls what should be displayed for the number of patients for the missing time point. Default to 0. For example, let us assume that there is no hemoglobin value for the patient in the Arm A group at time point 8:

 
hemoglobin_2 <- hemoglobin[!(hemoglobin$Arm == "Arm A" & hemoglobin$visit_nr == 8), ]


# numeric
boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin_2,
                var = hb,
                order = visit_nr,
                group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                group = Arm,
                main = "Boxplots for the two groups", 
                legend_position = "topleft", 
                missing_nr = 0)

Now let us imagine that there is no hemoglobin value for the patients in the Arm B group after timepoint 4:



hemoglobin_3 <- hemoglobin[!(hemoglobin$Arm == "Arm B" & hemoglobin$visit_nr > 4), ]


# numeric
boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin_3,
                var = hb,
                order = visit_nr,
                group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"), 
                group_names_short = c("A", "B"),
                group = Arm,
                main = "Boxplots for the two groups", 
                legend_position = "topleft", 
                missing_nr = NA)
